name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
notes: Adjacent cross-domain study with WebShop as its web evaluation. WebShop uses text-rendered search/product pages and an explicit valid-action menu, not screenshot control or live purchases. Fine-tuning and retrieval use collected training experience; the hybrid masks same-episode retrieval, which does not establish general contamination freedom. name: CUAVerifierBench
notes: Public Parquet configs separate trajectories from per-reviewer annotations. The card declares MIT. The two splits have different review stages: Online-Mind2Web includes blind and verifier-informed annotations, whereas the internal split is blind-only. This measures verifier agreement rather than agent task success.
summary: Human-annotated browser-agent trajectories for comparing automated task-success and process-quality verifiers against reviewer judgments.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Published task definitions include preconditions and clarification requirements; the metadata review does not independently validate the reported agent scores.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The card describes 140 single-app and 10 cross-app tasks. Task and app counts are different units.

name: MobileGUI-VBench
notes: Public task files are available as JSONL and XLSX with documentation. The card explicitly declares Apache-2.0 for the dataset, despite having no license field in its YAML metadata. It identifies mobile apps without fixing an operating-system taxonomy; model scores are not imported.
summary: Mobile-app task definitions covering everyday scenarios, with annotated preconditions and clarification requirements for evaluating agent behavior.

name: RecreationBench
notes: Dataset card declares multiple upstream licenses; do not treat the package as having one blanket permissive license.
summary: Tasks for recreating reference applications with hybrid computer interaction.
